statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-35189 ("Excessive Memory Allocation in Relative CRLDP Processing", Low) affects OpenSSL 3.5: a certificate with many nameRelativeToCRLIssuer CRL distribution points makes OpenSSL allocate several hundred MiB while caching X.509 extensions, so a malicious peer can cause memory pressure and possibly a denial of service in clients, or in servers that request client certificates. OpenSSL fixed it in 3.5.9, and Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 (DSA-6531-1) and in 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260929.txt, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-35189. The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64 (25 versions). No build of Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-35189. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, the fixed boundary here, and every later build carry the fix: the other rebuilds of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and its FIPS build carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 entry naming CVE-2026-35189, and the rebuilds of Debian 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 and its FIPS build are based on OpenSSL 3.5.9, and their changelog's 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 entry names CVE-2026-35189. Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the same OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory states the FIPS module is not affected because the affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
